commitMessage:
Bug 470244 - Replace new Boolean with Boolean.valueOf

Using `new Boolean()` results in the creation of a new object on the
heap, when the flyweight `Boolean.TRUE` and `Boolean.FALSE` are available.
Java 1.4 added a `Boolean.valueOf()` which can be used in place of
`new Boolean()` but which will use the existing flyweight values instead.

Globally change `new Boolean(...)` to `Boolean.valueOf(...)` and replace
constant valued expressions with their flyweight counterparts.

Bug: 470244
Change-Id: I608c1acf8b35274e3e8325de8d396f2d077001ce
Signed-off-by: Alex Blewitt <alex.blewitt@gmail.com>
summary: Replaced `new Boolean(...)` with `Boolean.valueOf(...)`.

commitMessage:
Bug 487095 - Move test bundles to JUnit 4

Change-Id: I1c249f6ccc23850c0cf3e992ff7f5805f44b7585
Signed-off-by: Sopot Cela <scela@redhat.com>
dslRule:
<!id: junit3.to.junit4.add.test>
<!description: Add @Test annotation to JUnit 3 public test methods within classes extending TestCase, for migration to JUnit 4.>
<!severity: INFO>

void $name($params$) :: methodNameMatches($name, "test.*")
                     :: !isStatic($name)
                     :: hasModifier($name, "PUBLIC")
                     :: enclosingClassExtends("junit.framework.TestCase")
=> @org.junit.Test void $name($params$)
;;
summary: Adds the @org.junit.Test annotation to public instance methods whose names start with 'test' in classes that extend junit.framework.TestCase, facilitating migration from JUnit 3 to JUnit 4.
